title: Modelling by access pattern instead of by entity

videos.script: A relational schema starts from the things that exist. Customers, orders, lines, products. Each fact once. {{entities}} The questions come later, from anybody, and the join and the planner answer them. That is why the habit works there. {{join}} The stores in this course spread data across machines. A join across machines is a network trip for every row. So they give it up, or make it expensive. {{network}} The questions have to move. From read time, to design time. {{move}} So the design starts with a list. Every question the shop asks, what it already knows when it asks, and how often. {{list}} Then each question gets a home. In MongoDB, an order with its lines inside, and the customer by reference. {{mongo}} In Cassandra, one table per question, sorted the way the page reads it. And a key that loses an order without a word. {{cassandra}} In Redis, the key name is the query. And you will time the one command that stops the server for everyone. {{redis}} By the end, the list is a contract. The next question costs a new structure, and lesson 4 pays for it.
